name_en: Futatabi dango — mugwort dumplings kneaded twice for an extra-soft, fluffy texture
summary_ja: だんご粉を練って蒸し、摘みたてのよもぎを加えてもう一度つき直す延岡市のおやつ。通常一度きりの練りを「再び」おこなうことが名の由来で、あんを包んできな粉をまぶすと、若草色のやわらかな団子になる。
summary_en: Dumpling flour is kneaded, steamed with freshly picked mugwort folded in, then pounded a second time — a Nobeoka treat named for that unusual second working of the dough, wrapped around sweet bean paste and dusted with soybean flour into a soft, pale-green dumpling.
source_title: ふたたびだんご 宮崎県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Iriko mochi — a bar of soft mochi made from parched, ground glutinous rice
summary_ja: もち米を炒って粉にした「いり粉」を水飴で練り上げ、寝かせてから棒状に切る宮崎の菓子。江戸期に薩摩藩から伝わった節句菓子とされ、子どもの成長を願って近所に配る風習があったと伝わる。
summary_en: Glutinous rice is parched and ground into iriko flour, then kneaded with starch syrup, rested, and cut into bars — a Miyazaki sweet said to have arrived from the Satsuma domain as a festival treat, once handed out to neighbors to wish for a child's healthy growth.
source_title: いりこもち 宮崎県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Meno mochi arare — small-New-Year rice offerings later fried into crackers
summary_ja: 小正月に紅白や黄・緑に色づけた餅を榎の枝に刺して飾る「めの餅」を、1月30日頃に外して油で揚げてつくる南九州のあられ。繭の豊産を祈る「繭の餅」が語源とされ、五穀豊穣や厄払いの願いがこめられている。
summary_en: Small rice-cake offerings — dyed red-and-white, yellow, and green — are skewered onto an elm branch for Little New Year in a display called meno mochi; around January 30th they come down and are fried into crackers. The name is said to trace to a wish for a bountiful silkworm harvest, carrying hopes for good crops and warding off misfortune.
source_title: めの餅あられ 宮崎県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Nerikuri — pounded sweet potato and mochi, rolled in sweetened soybean flour
summary_ja: 蒸した甘藷（さつまいも）と餅をすり鉢でついて丸め、きな粉をまぶす都城市の菓子。正月の餅つきの最後の一臼に煮た甘藷を加えてつくったのがはじまりとされ、「ねりくり」は宮崎弁で「つきまぜる」の意という。
summary_en: Steamed sweet potato and mochi are pounded together in a mortar, shaped, and rolled in sweetened soybean flour — a Miyakonojo sweet said to have begun as the last batch of a New Year's mochi-pounding session, with simmered sweet potato worked in; nerikuri is Miyazaki dialect for pounding and mixing together.
source_title: ねりくり／ねったぼ／芋もち 宮崎県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省
